newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss help French probe Eurotunnel deals.
newsitem.headline: Swiss help French probe Eurotunnel deals.

text.p: Switzerland has agreed to help French authorities probe possible insider trading in shares of Eurotunnel ahead of the company's 1994 capital increase, the justice ministry in Berne said on Thursday.
A spokesman for the Federal Police Agency (BAP) confirmed media reports that Switzerland had agreed to support a French request for legal assistance in the probe by Paris prosecutors.
"The reports are correct," BAP spokesman Folco Galli said, confirming the French request had arrived on June 14 and that the matter was now in the hands of Geneva prosecutors.

The investigation centres on three Swiss banks in Geneva and Zurich, Facts magazine said, adding French authorities suspect they used their knowledge of the impending capital increase to sell shares before the price fell drastically.
The share price fell by half after the issue of new stock in June 1994 to help cover cost overruns incurred in building a rail link under the English Channel.
"The request seeks documents, but the French are also demanding that people involved be questionned," Galli said. He would not identify the targets in the probe.
French stock market watchdog COB said in March it had found no evidence of insider trading in Eurotunnel shares after carrying out an investigation into allegations made against unnamed institutions.
But it said it had advised the institutions involved to strengthen internal controls involving confidential matters.
